question: Should OpenClaw Core own a durable Pi/Review/squash-promotion workflow and its contracts artifact, or should this live in an owner platform plugin/service using existing Core seams?
rationale: The answer determines the long-term security authority, deployment lifecycle, public contract, and compatibility model; it cannot be resolved safely by a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Keep orchestration outside Core
options.body: Move the service-specific workflow, contracts, and promotion policy to the owning platform plugin or service, adding only a generic Core seam if one is demonstrably required.

options.title: Sponsor a Core platform boundary
options.body: Approve a named Core owner, authorization model, public lifecycle/API contract, migration strategy, and end-to-end deployment proof before continuing this branch.

recommendation.title: Keep orchestration outside Core
recommendation.body: Move the service-specific workflow, contracts, and promotion policy to the owning platform plugin or service, adding only a generic Core seam if one is demonstrably required.

likelyOwner.reason: A Core-versus-owner-service boundary requires repository-level product and architecture sponsorship.
